title: Webhook URLs (with query-string secrets) and Vault key listings are echoed into the run output stream
existing_state: WebhookCommand emits the full request line including the substituted URL to the output stream: context.EmitOutput($"Webhook: {method} {url}", ScriptOutputType.Debug) (Services/Scripting/Commands/WebhookCommand.cs:100). Webhook URLs routinely carry secrets in the query string or path (Slack/Teams/PagerDuty tokens, signed URLs), so the secret is written verbatim into the same output channel the UI/history can display. Header values built from variables (e.g. Authorization) are substituted with no redaction (:72-73). Separately, Vault missing-key errors enumerate every field name in the secret into the exception message ('available keys: ...', Services/Vault/VaultService.cs:99-101, 136-139), which can flow into script output/history.
recommendation: Redact credentials from webhook debug output: log only scheme+host+path (strip query string and userinfo), or gate the full-URL log behind an explicit verbose/diagnostic flag. Do not include header values in any emitted output. For the Vault missing-key message, omit the enumerated key list (or gate it behind debug mode) so secret structure isn't leaked into history. Route both through the shared redaction helper proposed in SEC-002.
user_benefit: Prevents bearer tokens and signed webhook URLs from being persisted into run history and shown in debug panels where they can be exported or shoulder-surfed.

evidence.note: Full substituted URL emitted to output; header values substituted with no redaction
Missing-key error enumerates all secret field names
